notes: S6 ADDITION. WHAT A BROKER NEEDS BEFORE HE SAYS A WORD is the `needs` field, and the three of them are a gradient rather than a switch: `none` is a public bounty anybody may claim, `acquaintance` is a landlord who has to not dislike you, and `member` is a guild that has sworn you in - which is exactly what the Skyrunner questline graduates a player into. The owner's authored files are untouched; this one is new and every id in it is a cross-reference into content/raws/names/notables.json, content/raws/factions/factions.json and the five contraband goods the code names. A broker or a patron this file invents is refused at load, by name, so the board can never quietly grow a forty-third notable - and `bounty_rats` carries a DELIBERATE bad id, `nobody_at_all`, so that refusal is proved by a case rather than by the file happening to be correct. Do not remove it. WHAT A RADIANT CONTRACT IS HERE: the SHAPE is generated - which broker, which patron, how many, how long - and every NAME in it is authored. The brief is a template filled from the notables' own file, so a job always says who wants it, where they are, who lands it and where THEY are, and no two nights read the same. Payment is payPerUnit times units, moved by what the broker's own guild thinks of the player (guildPricePercent), so the ward's economy prices its own crime.

brokers.label: THE WARD'S BOUNTY
brokers.note: Watchman Cull keeps the impound and knows to the penny what the ward pays for what. A bounty is the only work on this board that is not a crime - which is why the man who hands it out is also the man who will take you for the rest of it.

brokers.label: THE HOUSE'S OWN WORK
brokers.note: Master Venn buys for his own cellar and asks nothing. A captains' house that only ever poured what the Weighhouse had stamped would be a captains' house with an empty cellar.

brokers.label: WORK OFF THE ROOFS
brokers.note: The quiet tenant brokers for the roofs. He does not offer anything to a stranger: the guild's first rung is what makes him say a word about work at all.

offers.brief: {patron} is overrun at {patronSite} and the ward pays by the scalp. {source} says the worst of them come up out of {sourceSite} after the doors shut.
Old Cobb's terriers cannot be everywhere. {patron} has asked the Watch for men at {patronSite}, and the Watch has asked whoever is drinking.
{patron} wants it at {patronSite} and does not want it weighed. {source} lands it at {sourceSite} on the night tide; the barrels are honest and the stamp on them is not.
There is a wedding at {patronSite} and {patron} has counted the jars twice. What {source} keeps at {sourceSite} is nobody's business until somebody writes it down.
{patron} keeps a back room at {patronSite} and the back room keeps a smell. It comes off {source}'s ground at {sourceSite} baled like hemp, because at four in the morning it looks like hemp.
One night only: {patron} has a room of men at {patronSite} who will pay tonight and be at sea tomorrow. {source} has it standing at {sourceSite} and will not hold it past the tide.

Light, small, and worth more than the boat it came on. {patron} takes delivery at {patronSite} and asks nothing; {source} has it off a hull at {sourceSite} and would rather not be seen holding it either.
Brann keeps two sets of books and the second one is short. {patron} is owed out of it at {patronSite}, and {source} at {sourceSite} is who it was owed from.

{patron} at {patronSite} will pay for {thing}, and will not ask which window it came out of. It is in {source}'s house at {sourceSite} and it is not insured, because insuring it would mean saying what it is.
things: a christening cup with two names filed off it
a sea-chart with the wrong soundings inked over the right ones
a signet nobody outside a guild should be able to press
a strongbox key that was cut twice

offers.brief: Salvage law says what comes off a wreck belongs to whoever holds it. {patron} holds a counter at {patronSite}; {source} holds {thing} at {sourceSite} and holds it wrongly.
things: a captain's glass with a dead man's initials on the barrel
a bond-paper that should have burned with the ship
a rosary of Flame-glass off a passenger nobody has claimed
